health.yellow: Data health: yellow (computed with a warning).
health.unknown: Data health: unknown (the run did not finish).

timing.next_open: Trade at the US open on {date}.
timing.next_close: Trade at the US close on {date}.
timing.same_close: Signal for the close of {date} (not achievable in practice).

timingPassed.next_open: This applied at the US open on {date}, which has already passed.
timingPassed.next_close: This applied at the US close on {date}, which has already passed.

dataYellow.title: {strategy}: data warning for {date}
dataYellow.body: The signal was computed, but some data has a warning. Allocation: {allocation}.

dataRed.title: {strategy}: safe state for {date}
dataRed.body: Data is not reliable enough for a normal signal, so the strategy's safe state applies.

provisional.title: {strategy}: data problem for {date}, re-checking
provisional.body: Data is not reliable enough for a normal signal yet. Saku checks it again every hour until {deadline} and then sends one final instruction.
provisional.fallback: If it is still not reliable then, the strategy's safe state applies. Safe-state target: {holdings}.
provisional.wait: Wait for the final instruction before trading on the signal of {date}; it arrives by {deadline}.

cleared.title: {strategy}: data cleared for {date}
cleared.body: The re-check found the data reliable, so the normal signal applies. This is the final instruction for {date}.

recheck.stands: The data was still not reliable at the last re-check before {deadline}, so the safe state stands. This is the final instruction for {date}.
recheck.late: Saku could not re-check the data before the deadline ({deadline}), so the safe state stands, as the provisional message said. This is the final instruction for {date}.
recheck.notRechecked: This day was graded too close to its re-check deadline ({deadline}) or after it, so it is not re-checked: this is the final instruction.

drill.body: This is a drill (pnpm drill): nothing was recorded, no data was changed and nothing needs to be done.

jobFailure.title: Saku: the {job} run for {date} did not finish
jobFailure.more: ...and {count} more. The full list is in the run's error (job_runs.error) and the job log on the server.
jobFailure.body: It runs again at the next hourly check. The job log on the server has the details.

alerts.test: Saku: this channel works. Alerts will arrive here.

dataAdmin.title: Saku: data for {date} is not green
dataAdmin.body: Not green: {reasons}. Each strategy states its own status; a red one applies its safe state.

disk.title: Saku: the server disk is {percent}% full
disk.body: {free} is free and the database is {size}. Prune old backups and logs to free space (docs/troubleshooting.md).

audit.title: Saku: audit report for {month}
audit.days: Trading days: {green} green, {yellow} yellow, {red} red, {notGraded} not graded.
audit.daysUnknown: Trading days: not known (the market calendar does not cover the month).
audit.revisions: Revisions: {revisions} stored bar values changed, {readjustments} provider re-adjustments.
audit.quota: Quota: {over} of {providers} providers above 80% of a limit.
audit.quotaPartial: Quota: {over} of {providers} providers above 80% of a limit; the counts are incomplete (the earliest days are no longer stored).
audit.forward: Forward records: chains verified; {entries} entries, {safe} safe-state days, {missing} days missing, {annotations} annotations.
audit.forwardBroken: Forward records: chain verification found {problems} problems; {entries} entries, {safe} safe-state days, {missing} days missing, {annotations} annotations.
audit.runs: Runs: {runs}, of which {failed} failed or did not finish.
audit.full: The full report is on the server: {command}

update.title: Saku: the update to {to} failed at the {step} step
update.back: The server went back to {from} and keeps running it. It tries again when a newer version is pushed; the update log on the server has the details.
update.stuck: Going back to {from} failed too, so the jobs may not run. Run ops/update-server.sh on the server by hand.

check.bar_valid: a bar failed the basic checks ({source})
check.unchanged_close: the close did not change, possibly stale ({source})
check.large_move: an unusually large move to confirm ({source})
check.secondary_missing: no bar from {source} for this day
check.adj_return_match: adjusted returns differ from the provider ({source})
check.dividend_pending: a dividend is not listed by {source} yet and no other secondary source confirmed it
check.leverage_track: the fund does not track its leverage of the underlying ({source})
check.index_match: the fund does not track its index ({source})
check.index_unavailable: the index check could not run: the index has no value for the day ({source})
check.fx_unavailable: the exchange rate cross-check could not run: the main source has no rate for the day ({source})

issuer.nav_premium: the market close is further from the issuer's NAV than usual ({source})
issuer.distribution_match: distributions differ from the issuer's records ({source})
issuer.split_match: splits differ from the issuer's records ({source})
issuer.issuer_stale: the issuer's NAV is missing or more than one trading day old ({source})
issuer.nav_tolerance_invalid: the NAV tolerance setting is invalid, so premiums are only observed ({source})

reason.primary_missing: the main source has no data and no stand-in passed
reason.decision_margin: a stand-in price is too close to a signal threshold
reason.standIn: the main source was missing; {source} stands in
reason.standInRefused: the main source was missing and no stand-in passed the checks
reason.standInClosedChanged: a stand-in an admin had closed now has another price (from {source}); it is checked again as an unconfirmed price
reason.closedDayEvent: a dividend or split is dated {date}, a day the market was closed; it is in no price the signals read, so the fund's returns from then on cannot be trusted until the source corrects it or an admin resolves it
reason.standInLookback: the signals read a secondary source's price for {date}, not yet confirmed by the main source
reason.lookbackRed: the data of {date}, which the signals still read, is red (unreliable)
reason.lookbackUngraded: the data of {date}, which the signals still read, has not been checked
reason.lookbackMissing: the price of {date}, which the signals still read, is missing
reason.issuerUnavailable: issuer data could not be fetched ({source})
reason.issuer_nav_tolerance_invalid: the issuer NAV tolerance setting is invalid; reset it (pnpm settings set issuer_nav_tolerance)
reason.evaluation: the strategy could not be evaluated
reason.rangeMissing: {indicator} has no value: the open, high or low of {date} is missing (never estimated)
reason.rangeInvalid: {indicator} has no value: the open, high, low and close of {date} do not fit together (outside the day's range, or not positive)
reason.valueInvalid: {indicator} has no value: a price of {date} it reads is not positive or not a number
reason.warmUp: {indicator} has no value yet: not enough history (warm-up)

recompute.title: Saku: the engine now decides {count} recorded days differently
recompute.body: First: {version} on {date}, recorded {recorded}, now {now}; signals that differ: {signals}. Recorded entries stay as they are; each difference is annotated. Find the cause before trusting new signals.
recompute.others: Other recorded days now decided differently:

standInCorrected.title: {strategy}: correction to the signal of {date}
standInCorrected.body: The signal of {date} used a secondary price for {ticker}; the primary's price, which arrived later, differed from it by {deviation}.
standInCorrected.earlier: The signal of {date} read a secondary price for {ticker} on {standInDate}; the primary's price, which arrived later, differed from it by {deviation}.
standInCorrected.differs: Recorded allocation: {recorded}. With the corrected price it would have been {corrected}. The record is annotated, not changed.
standInCorrected.same: Recorded allocation: {recorded}. With the corrected price it would have been the same: the signal would not have changed.
standInCorrected.otherChanged: Other days the corrected price would have changed:
standInCorrected.more: Other corrections of this strategy that would not have changed the signal: {count} (each is annotated in the record).
standInCorrected.afterClose: The primary's price arrived after an admin had closed this stand-in as never to be replaced; it is compared all the same.
standInCorrected.pastDay: This is about a past day, not a new signal: the latest signal gives the current allocation.

standInUnreadable.title: Saku: a stand-in correction annotation cannot be read
standInUnreadable.body: {version}, {date}: annotation {id} does not read back, so its correction is not told. The record is unchanged; find the cause.

standInClosed.title: {strategy}: {ticker}'s price for {standInDate} stays a secondary price
standInClosed.titleResolved: {strategy}: {ticker}'s stand-in for {standInDate} was closed, then the primary's price arrived
standInClosed.body: The primary source will not deliver {ticker}'s price for {standInDate}, so an admin closed its stand-in: the secondary source's price stays, and no primary price will check it.
standInClosed.bodyResolved: The primary source was expected not to deliver {ticker}'s price for {standInDate}, so an admin closed its stand-in; the primary's price arrived later after all and was compared with it (a difference is told as a correction).
standInClosed.bodyChanged: The primary source will not deliver {ticker}'s price for {standInDate}, so an admin closed its stand-in; since then the day has another secondary price, which is checked again as an unconfirmed price.
standInClosed.days: Recorded days that used it: {count} ({first} to {last}). Their signals stay as recorded; the record is annotated, not changed.
standInClosed.from: From now on, signals read this price as it is: it no longer makes a day yellow or red as an unconfirmed price.
standInClosed.pastDay: This is not a new signal: the latest signal gives the current allocation.

standInReopened.title: Saku: the closed stand-in of {ticker} on {date} has another price
standInReopened.body: An admin closed the stand-in at {closed} from {closedSource}; the checks now build the day from {now} from {source}. It is open again: checked as an unconfirmed price and holding corrections back. Check the new price, then close it again: pnpm sources stand-in close {ticker} {date} --reason "<text>" --user <admin>.
standInReopened.refused: An admin closed the stand-in at {closed} from {closedSource}; the checks now refuse the day (no canonical bar, the day reads as missing). It is open again and holds corrections back until the primary delivers the day.

standInClosedUnreadable.title: Saku: a stand-in close annotation cannot be read
standInClosedUnreadable.body: {version}, {date}: annotation {id} does not read back, so its close is not told. The record is unchanged; find the cause.

revisions.title: Saku: the weekly refetch changed {count} stored values
revisions.body: Changed: {items}. The old values are kept in the revision log; checks and recorded days were recomputed with the new ones (any recorded day now decided differently is sent separately).
revisions.withdrawn: Withdrawn by the source: {items}. The source no longer has a value for these dates. The old values stay in the revision log but are not used from the withdrawal on (those dates read as missing, never as 0); checks and recorded days were recomputed without them (any recorded day now decided differently is sent separately).

integrity.title: Saku: a calculation check failed ({check})
integrity.body: {detail}. The two calculations must agree; find the cause before trusting new signals.

parity.title: Saku: a testfol parity case failed ({name})
parity.body: {detail}. The case is backtested with same_close execution, which is not achievable: it trades at a close that is not yet known (used only for this comparison). Saku's backtest must match testfol's within the documented tolerances; find the cause and record it in docs/parity.md before trusting backtests. Tolerances are never widened to pass.

healthGrade.unknown: Data health: unknown (the run did not finish).

price.name: Price
price.tooltip: The fund's value at the day's close: the plain price (adjusted for splits) or, with total return, a level that also counts reinvested dividends.
price.why: Most rules compare today's value with something slower, such as its own average.
price.example: Price above its 200-day average: the fund is in an uptrend.

sma.name: Simple moving average (SMA)
sma.tooltip: The plain average of the last N closing values. It needs N days of data before it has a value (warm-up).
sma.why: It smooths out daily noise, so a rule reacts to the trend rather than to one day.
sma.example: SMA 200 = the average of the last 200 closes.

ema.name: Exponential moving average (EMA)
ema.tooltip: An average of past closing values that gives recent days more weight. It starts as the plain average of the first N days, then each day moves 2 / (N + 1) of the way toward the new value.
ema.why: It reacts to a turn sooner than a plain average of the same length, at the cost of more false alarms.
ema.example: EMA 20: today's close counts about 10%, yesterday's EMA the other 90%.
ema.history: It depends on every value since the first stored day, so a longer stored history can change it slightly.

return.name: Return over N days
return.tooltip: How much the value changed over the last N trading days, in percent: (today / N days ago - 1) x 100.
return.why: Momentum: funds that rose over recent months have tended to keep rising for a while, though not always.
return.example: Return 126 above 0%: the fund is higher than about six months ago.

volatility.name: Volatility
volatility.tooltip: How much the value swings, as a yearly percentage (daily swings x the square root of 252 trading days). The method decides which prices of each day are used.
volatility.why: Calm markets have tended to reward holding risk; very volatile ones are where large losses happen.
volatility.example: Volatility 20 below 25%: the last 20 days were calm.

volatilityClose.name: Close-to-close volatility
volatilityClose.tooltip: The spread (sample standard deviation) of the last N daily returns from close to close, per year, in percent. The default method.
volatilityClose.why: The simplest and most widely used measure; it needs only closing prices.
volatilityClose.example: Daily moves of about 1% give roughly 16% a year.

volatilityParkinson.name: Parkinson volatility
volatilityParkinson.tooltip: Volatility from each day's high and low instead of the closes, per year, in percent. It needs every day's high and low; a day without them gives no value.
volatilityParkinson.why: The day's range holds more information than one close, so it settles faster with fewer days. It does not see overnight gaps.
volatilityParkinson.example: A day trading between 99 and 101 adds about a 2% range.

volatilityGarmanKlass.name: Garman-Klass volatility
volatilityGarmanKlass.tooltip: Volatility from each day's open, high, low and close, per year, in percent. It needs all four prices every day; a day without them gives no value.
volatilityGarmanKlass.why: It uses more of each day's prices than the close or the range alone, so it is steadier. It does not see overnight gaps.
volatilityGarmanKlass.example: Used like close-to-close volatility, for example below 25% as a calm signal.

volatilityYangZhang.name: Yang-Zhang volatility
volatilityYangZhang.tooltip: Volatility that combines overnight gaps (previous close to open), the open-to-close move and the day's range, per year, in percent. It needs every day's open, high and low.
volatilityYangZhang.why: It counts overnight gaps that the range methods miss, which matters on news days.
volatilityYangZhang.example: A fund that jumps at the open after news shows higher Yang-Zhang than Parkinson volatility.

drawdown.name: Drawdown
drawdown.tooltip: How far today's value is below its highest value, in percent (0% at a new high). The high is over the last N days, or since the first stored day when no length is set (all-time high).
drawdown.why: It shows how deep the current fall is; many rules step aside after a deep fall or wait for a recovery.
drawdown.example: Drawdown -10%: the fund is 10% below its high.
drawdown.history: Without a length it depends on every value since the first stored day.

high.name: N-day high
high.tooltip: The highest closing value of the last N days, today included (closes, not the day's intraday highs).
high.why: A close at a new N-day high is a classic breakout signal.
high.example: Price at its 50-day high: no close in the last 50 days was higher.

low.name: N-day low
low.tooltip: The lowest closing value of the last N days, today included (closes, not the day's intraday lows).
low.why: A close at a new N-day low is a classic breakdown signal, often used to step aside.
low.example: Price at its 20-day low: no close in the last 20 days was lower.

threshold.name: Fixed level
threshold.tooltip: A fixed number to compare with, for example a volatility of 25 (percent). Plain prices, averages, highs and lows cannot be compared with a fixed level, because a split would change what it means.
threshold.why: Percentages such as return, volatility and drawdown mean the same at any price, so a fixed level works for them.
threshold.example: Drawdown below -20: the fund is more than 20% below its high.

glossary.warmUp: Warm-up: the days an indicator needs before it has its first value. A 200-day average has none until 200 days of data exist; no signal is given before then.
glossary.totalReturn: Total return: the value of the fund with its dividends reinvested on the ex-dividend date (the first day the price no longer includes them), not only the price.
glossary.annualized: Per year (annualized): daily volatility scaled to a year with the square root of 252 trading days, so periods of any length compare.
glossary.intradayPrices: Open, high and low: the day's first trade, highest and lowest price. Some volatility methods need them; a day without them gives no value, never an estimate.
glossary.allTimeHigh: All-time high: the highest value since the first day Saku stores for the fund, not necessarily the fund's first trading day.
